referenceList.doiPolicy: DOIs are rendered as full https://doi.org/ URLs when the entry has one, matching docx-tools' APA 7 renderer.

provenance.claim: mode: author-year with an APA-7-shaped reference template — docx-tools' default citation_style is "apa" (src/docx_tools/build.py, DEFAULT_CITATION_STYLE) and its APA renderer emits "Author, A. A., & Author, B. B. (Year). Title. Journal, volume(issue), pages. https://doi.org/…" (src/docx_tools/bib.py).
widthPresetsMm.single = 127 mm — docx-tools inserts figures at a default width of 5.0 inches (src/docx_tools/build.py: default_w = 3.0 if float_side else 5), which is 127 mm.

minDpi = 600 is OUR OWN requirement, not a journal's: SUNA figures are authored as vector SVG, so a raster pass is only ever a rendering of something sharper, and we would rather an internal PDF read cleanly on a high-DPI screen and in print than match the 300 dpi floor journals set for supplied artwork.
palette/panelLabel values are SUNA house defaults, not a journal requirement: this is a drafting style, so it recommends the colourblind-safe Wong ramp rather than mandating anything.

Single-spaced, no line numbers, page numbers on: SUNA style is read on a screen or printed for ourselves, not marked up by reviewers — double spacing and line numbers exist to leave room for a reviewer's pen and to let one cite "page 4, line 12", and neither buys anything internally. Page numbers stay because a printed internal report gets dropped on a desk.
acceptedFileTypes docx/pdf/html are exactly the three formats SUNA itself exports — for a house style this field describes what we hand each other, not what a submission portal will take.

No required sections and no limits of any kind: this is a house drafting style, not a journal, so it must never flag a manuscript for a rule nobody stated. Limits arrive when the author switches to a journal profile.

notes: SUNA style is OUR OWN invented house style — an internal design, not a transcription of anybody's author guidelines. Every rule in it was chosen by us, for how we draft and circulate work; nothing here is evidence of what a journal wants, and its `sources` are empty on purpose. Switch to a journal profile before submission to get that journal's actual rules.

What it does state: single spacing, no line numbers, page numbers on, figures at 600 dpi minimum, and docx / pdf / html as the formats we exchange. What it deliberately does NOT state: any word, abstract, title, display-item or reference limit, any required section, any availability statement — so a draft in progress is never flagged for being unfinished. Its three article types (draft manuscript, letter, internal report) are the three documents we actually write.

Its typography reproduces the structure `docx-tools build` produces, so an export from SUNA and one from the docx-tools CLI lay out the same: US Letter, 0.5 in margins, Times New Roman 11 pt at 1.15 line spacing, 14 pt bold centred title, 8 pt author line with superscript affiliation markers, 9 pt centred affiliations, 13 pt black H1 (Word's Heading 1 is blue by default — docx-tools forces black and so does SUNA style), figure captions BELOW the image with a bold 'Figure N.' and italic body, table captions ABOVE with APA rules only, and a 0.5 in hanging indent on the reference list.
The page break after the front matter is docx-tools' behaviour too (build.py inserts one before the first heading that follows the front matter unless that heading is the Abstract).
